newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks slump as foreigners turn to Dow.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks slump as foreigners turn to Dow.

text.p: Mexican stocks fell for the fourth straight session Tuesday, hurt by investor interest in the U.S. markets, traders and analysts said.

"The market is very quiet again. Foreign investors have yet to step in, I think they're still wary of Mexico due to political factors and because the Dow is still rallying," said Daniel Romo, equity analyst at the Bancrecer financial group.
The blue chip IPC index fell 8.06 points to 3,358.16. Volume was a lackluster 72.5 million shares.
The Dow Jones industrial average rose 50.69 points to 6,397.60, its 40th record close this year.
"As long as the party goes on in New York, they won't even turn to look at us, and unless they do, things here won't change," said a floor trader.
Although stocks closed down, they were off lows and respected resistance at 3,350 points, analysts noted.
"It rebounded near support again, and the winter rally could begin from these levels," Romo said.
A total of 104 stocks were traded, of which losers outnumbered gainers by 50 to 28.
Financial stock Abacogf A series headed the gainers, up 20 ($0.03) centavos to 2.80 pesos ($0.35), but at moderate trade, dealers noted.
Small autoparts maker Iasasa A series shares headed the losers, down four centavos ($0.01) to 41 ($0.05), but at minimal volume.
